judged_text: The Salesforce service now performs an unconditional token-refresh POST to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update on every service construction, where the jsforce connection previously refreshed lazily only when the stored access token was rejected. Every availability check and booking against a Salesforce credential now pays an extra OAuth round-trip and a credential DB write (Salesforce token endpoints are rate-limited), and a transient refresh failure that previously only affected an expired token now aborts all Salesforce operations whose stored token was still valid.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now unconditionally performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then immediately `prisma.credential.update(...)` before constructing/returning the `jsforce.Connection` (see the newly added `fetch(...)` + `await prisma.credential.update(...)` block right after `const credentialKey = ...`). Any transient refresh failure (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`) will now abort Salesforce operations even if the previously stored `access_token` might still be valid, and every instantiation incurs an extra OAuth call and DB write. This behavior change is directly shown by the diff and can cause real operational failures (rate limits / availability) beyond a mere optimization concern.
